---
applyTo: "packages/genui/ui-judge/**/*"
---

Keep UI Judge a Rust-only crate. Its public API, model integration, tests, and user examples belong under `packages/genui/ui-judge`; do not add an npm package manifest, TypeScript facade, or JavaScript test suite back to this directory. The default feature set remains library-only. The `server` feature owns the `ui-judge-server` binary and HTTP process adapter. The existing ReactLynx fixture source is a runtime asset consumed by the repository's headless runner, not a JavaScript UI Judge API or test harness.

Keep the default crate-root API restricted to `judge_page`, `JudgePageRequest`, `UiJudgeResult`, and `UiJudgeError`; the `server` feature may additionally expose its server module. The request uses only standard-library field types and always performs visual-correctness scoring internally. `JudgePageRequest::include_geqi` may additionally run the four weighted GEQI dimensions against the same final screenshot; keep their identifiers, labels, criteria, order, and weights internal rather than exporting dimension-selection or prompt APIs. Do not export model clients, model options, runner types, screenshot helpers, prompts, parsers, GEQI dimension types, fixture helpers, or screenshot-comparison APIs.

Keep the feature-gated server protocol at `GET /health`, `POST /judge`, `POST /screenshot`, `POST /screenshot/zip`, and `POST /compare`. The JSON screenshot route accepts the same request as `/judge`, returns the captured frame transcoded to `image/jpeg`, and skips VLM scoring, GEQI, and reference-image comparison. It must reuse the bounded headless capture queue; avoid model initialization when `steps` is empty, and use Agent SDK only to execute non-empty natural-language steps. The ZIP screenshot route accepts only a raw `application/zip` body, fixes its entrypoint to `zip:///index.lynxml`, returns `image/jpeg` with `Cache-Control: no-store`, and must not accept a filename, URL, entrypoint, base directory, model option, or interaction step. Reserve one of the four ZIP staging slots before buffering the body, apply a ten-second total body-read deadline, enforce 10 MiB while reading even when `Content-Length` is absent or false, inject the canonical extraction directory internally, and move its `ExtractedZip` guard and staging permit into the queued capture job so request cancellation cannot delete resources still in use and no more than four staged trees exist. Keep the public library and JSON routes restricted to `file://`, `http://`, and `https://`. The comparison route accepts exactly one `referenceImage` and one `renderedImage` multipart upload, applies the existing image limits, and runs only deterministic normalization, alignment, and pixel comparison; it must not initialize a model client or enqueue headless rendering. Read `LYNX_USE_PORT` with a default of `8080`, reject zero, and bind separate IPv4 and IPv6 unspecified listeners. Have `build.rs` generate an executable `start.sh` in the Cargo profile output directory that starts the colocated `ui-judge-server` binary, copy the target Lynx runtime and `lynx_core.js` into the same runnable output layout, and package those generated assets rather than recovering them independently in `build.sh`. Obtain the default core script through the shared, SHA-256-verified artifact downloader rather than a checked-in fixture; honor `LYNX_CORE_JS_PATH` as a local build-time source while retaining the platform-standard packaged destination name. The server binary should select the packaged runtime when the caller has not set `LYNX_LIB_PATH` or `LYNX_SDK_DIR`, so the launcher stays a simple colocated executable wrapper. Accept HTTP connections concurrently, but run every native page lifecycle sequentially through one process-wide capture broker shared by `judge_page` and the server; its dedicated owner thread reuses one `LynxContainer`. Do not reintroduce a `LocalSet`, a `JoinSet` of capture futures, multiple production capture brokers, or multiple native container owners. Use a bounded capture queue, enqueue synchronously so backpressure is reported before a caller waits for the owner, purge cancelled jobs before returning `503` for a full queue, and return `503` when no live slot remains. The owner worker may bridge to the async model client with one current-thread runtime; that is the only async allowed on the native side. After capture returns an owned BMP, run VLM scoring and reference comparison concurrently across judge requests. Limit request bodies and gracefully drain the HTTP server and join the headless worker on SIGINT or SIGTERM. Treat a headless-worker panic as fatal: atomically stop admission, drop queued jobs so their handlers can drain, mark readiness unhealthy, initiate shutdown, and propagate the join failure from the server task.

Keep untrusted ZIP staging in the server-feature `src/zip/` module and never accept a client-supplied extraction directory. Reject uploads above 10 MiB before parsing, archives with more than 100 entries, overlapping entries, encryption, unsafe or duplicate paths, path/file collisions, symlinks and non-file/non-directory Unix types. Do not rely only on `ZipArchive::len()` for the count or duplicate checks: `zip` 8.6 stores entries by raw name and silently replaces exact duplicates, so also validate the structural central-directory entry count. Before constructing `ZipArchive`, accept only the rightmost classic EOCD whose comment ends exactly at EOF, reject ZIP64 sentinels and ZIP64 local or central extra fields, and structurally prove that the central directory ends at that EOCD with no more than 100 entries. Hide local headers and file data from the library's metadata fallback scan and reject extra EOCD signatures in the visible central-directory and comment region, so a malformed outer record cannot fall back to metadata embedded in an ordinary nested ZIP. Limit each file to 50 MiB, the archive output to 100 MiB, path depth to 20, components to 255 bytes, relative paths to 4096 bytes, and both declared and actually written compression ratios to 100:1. Extract through a fixed 64 KiB buffer into a fresh private `TempDir`, create files exclusively, count actual writes, propagate CRC/read failures, and remove the complete staging directory on every failure. Nested ZIP files remain ordinary files.

Run synchronous ZIP work through `spawn_blocking` with a separate four-permit semaphore and a ten-second absolute deadline. Reject immediately rather than queue when all four permits are occupied, and reserve that same capacity in the HTTP adapter before buffering another upload. A timed-out blocking task cannot be forcibly stopped, so move its permit and temporary-directory guard into the blocking closure and check the same deadline between entries, reads, and writes; do not release capacity when only the async join wait times out. A successful `ExtractedZip` must retain that permit for its whole staged-tree lifetime. ZIP-backed capture must inject the canonical base directory internally and move the extraction guard and permit into the queued capture job so request cancellation cannot delete resources still in use and queued captures cannot exceed the four-tree disk bound. Deployment must add the hard containment Rust cannot provide: a non-root account, read-only root filesystem, and a dedicated `noexec,nosuid,nodev` temporary volume with an ephemeral-storage quota sized for four bounded extractions. Record only sanitized archive byte/entry/declared-size/actual-size/duration/outcome metrics plus a trusted job identity, never raw entry names or free-form tasks.

The runner captures frames as uncompressed BMP. Keep that lossless copy for the deterministic reference comparison and transcode to JPEG only for bytes that leave the process — the VLM data URL and the `/screenshot` response — because vision models do not accept `image/bmp`. Composite transparent pixels over white when transcoding.

Keep reference-image comparison inside the Rust crate and reachable through `JudgePageRequest::reference_image`. Preserve `reference` as textual model context; accept reference images as plain base64, base64 data URLs, or HTTP(S) URLs, with explicit compressed-byte, decoded-dimension, pixel-count, and allocation limits. After the final screenshot is captured, run the VLM evaluations and reference-image comparison as independent chains that share only the captured frame. Every VLM evaluation always scores that single screenshot from `task` and textual `reference`; never send the reference image, alignment result, pixel diff, or deterministic similarity to a VLM. The reference-image chain must only load and normalize the baseline, align it with normalized cross-correlation, and compute block-based pixel differences and a diff image. Run bounded alignment and pixel-diff work off the async runtime. Keep top-level `score`, `reason`, and `summary` owned by the visual-correctness VLM; keep each GEQI dimension's score, reason, summary, and error independent, preserve the 30/25/15/15 relative weighting normalized to a 0-100 result, and do not let a dimension failure overwrite the visual-correctness result. Report reference-image failures separately without overwriting VLM output, and preserve successful comparison diagnostics when VLM scoring fails. Expose only standard-type diagnostics on `UiJudgeResult`; keep alignment, comparison, artifact, prompt, and algorithm types private to the crate.

Preserve the former TypeScript reference-comparison semantics during migration work: successful alignment compares the overlap crop, fallback comparison normalizes both images to their minimum dimensions with fill-style resizing, and pixel distance compares all four raw RGBA channels. Penalizing non-overlap or premultiplying alpha is a separate metric change, not a migration cleanup. Run CPU-heavy post-capture image work, including BMP-to-JPEG transcoding, on a bounded Rayon pool off the async runtime. Keep a permit with each Rayon job until the CPU work actually ends, even if its async waiter is dropped, so cancelled requests cannot overbook the pool.

Do not modify or duplicate `lynx-headless-rust-test-runner` as part of UI Judge work. `judge_page` must accept only `file://`, `http://`, and `https://` URLs; reject bare paths and other schemes before initializing the model or headless runtime. Internally use the runner's existing navigation, DOM, selector tap, wait, and software screenshot APIs. Keep model creation inside `judge_page` and the container and page lifecycle inside the single-owner capture worker. Do not re-export `LynxContainer`, `LynxPage`, or other runner implementation types or require callers to construct them. `judge_page` must stay callable from any runtime, including a current-thread one, because native work never runs on the caller's thread. Preserve natural-language `steps` by using Agent SDK to choose selector taps and waits from the current DOM and screenshot; report swipe, scrolling, typing, and coordinate touch as unsupported because the existing runner does not expose them. Do not add Kitten-Lynx, Android, ADB, an emulator, Playwright, or a browser as a UI Judge runtime dependency.

Keep `JudgePageRequest::timeout` compatible with the former TypeScript API: it is a per-operation and per-step limit, not an overall request deadline. Connection, navigation, each natural-language step, final screenshot capture, visual-correctness scoring, each enabled GEQI dimension, and optional reference-image comparison each receive the full duration; document that distinction wherever the request API is shown.

Use Agent SDK for structured VLM evaluation. Keep any OpenAI-compatible transport adapter in Rust and use only the documented `UI_JUDGE_API_KEY`, `UI_JUDGE_BASE_URL`, `UI_JUDGE_MODEL`, `UI_JUDGE_API_STYLE`, and `UI_JUDGE_TIMEOUT_MS` model environment-variable inputs. Do not accept legacy Midscene- or OpenAI-prefixed variables, JSON init config, or model-family configuration, and do not add a Midscene runtime dependency. Keep unit tests deterministic with `UI_JUDGE_MODEL_RESPONSE_JSON`. The runtime-backed `headless_e2e` integration test is intentionally different: it must reject mock-response variables unconditionally. It must skip inside the test when `UI_JUDGE_API_KEY` is absent or empty; otherwise it must call the real model supplied through the injected model environment.

Keep 0-5 score normalization and typed page result structures in the Rust library. Keep top-level `score` as the backward-compatible visual-correctness result; expose the optional weighted aggregate separately as `geqi_score` from 0 through 100. Do not add result-file generation, a UI Judge PR-comment action, or a GitHub comment publishing workflow.

Keep concurrent-request coverage fixed-size and behavioral: submit four distinct fixture bundles concurrently through the production single-owner worker, validate each screenshot, and do not add duration, QPS, latency, or throughput assertions.

Keep the existing React Lynx fixture at `packages/genui/ui-judge/tests/fixtures/react`, because the unchanged headless runner reads that path. Build its `.lynx.bundle` into the ignored `.generated/` directory and never commit generated bundle binaries.
